The user asked on 2026-11-20 to "work on a1+ Unit 5 same all deal as before none stop all approved": A1+ 5.Y follows A1 5.Y with one step each, straight to Preview in batches, Gemini 2.5 Flash photos and ElevenLabs audio pre-approved, no per-lesson gates, reviewed in Preview. Five still-life photos at a market stall and a café counter, each with one thing and one price card ($3 apples, $5 oranges, $2 bananas, $4 strawberries, $10 cake), and Diego asking at the stall. The seller is never pictured, so the narrators voice question and price.

lesson.title: 5.8 How much are the apples?
lesson.unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
lesson.goal: Ask the price of more than one thing (How much are the apples?) and understand the answer (They're three dollars.), next to How much is …? It's ….
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.8 Prices: A1 asks How much is …? about one named thing and the seller answers It is … dollars; A1+ 5.8 asks about more than one thing with How much are the … ? and answers with They're … dollars., next to How much is the cake? It's ten dollars. In each photo one thing (a bag of apples, a basket of oranges, a bunch of bananas, a box of strawberries, a cake) stands behind its own price card. Here How much asks a price, after 5.4's How much milk is there? asked an amount. Prices stay at ten dollars or less; bigger numbers come in 5.12.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 5.8 How much is …?, dollars; A1+ 3.3 they're; A1+ 2.4 it's; A1 numbers one to ten; A1 5.1 fruit.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Join How much are (how-MUCH-ar) and stress the price in They're THREE dollars; do not require native-like speed.
